science-1.title: Physical science: explain before memorising

sections.heading: Use quantities precisely
sections.text: Force, energy, power, heat and temperature describe different things. A correct numerical answer needs units and a clearly defined system. Conservation laws help track transfers instead of treating energy as something that simply disappears. Friction can convert organised motion into internal energy; that does not mean the total energy has vanished.

sections.heading: Models connect observations
sections.text: Atomic and molecular models explain chemical reactions and material properties at a scale that cannot be inferred from appearance alone. A physical change and a chemical change are distinguished by what happens to substances, not merely whether a visible change occurs. Balance a reaction by conserving atoms rather than changing the chemical identity of a formula to make arithmetic easier.

sections.heading: From principle to application
sections.text: For light, draw the path and identify the interface. For electricity, identify the circuit and distinguish potential difference, current and resistance. For heat transfer, separate conduction, convection and radiation. Relating a principle to an appliance or environmental situation helps reveal misunderstandings that memorising a definition can conceal. Keep safety-related examples conceptual rather than giving instructions for experiments with mains electricity or hazardous chemicals.

rows: Capacity or transfer / rate of transfer
A powerful device does not necessarily run for longer.
Energy transfer / measure related to thermal state
Objects at the same temperature can contain different internal energies.
Visible change alone is not decisive.

terms.meaning: A quantity remains accounted for within the defined system and exchanges.
Change in propagation direction associated with a change in medium.
Opposition to current under specified conditions.

science-1.trap: Power and energy have different units and meanings.

practice.question: Why can a small high-power device use less energy than a low-power device?
practice.answer: Energy depends on power and operating time. A brief high-power use may consume less total energy than a lower-power device operating for many hours.

mcq: Which quantity describes a rate of energy transfer?
Power is energy transferred per unit time.

science-2.title: Life science: structure, function and evidence

sections.heading: Organise levels of explanation
sections.text: Cells, tissues, organs and organ systems describe different levels of organisation. A structure’s function should be explained through what it does and how it interacts with other parts. Plants and animals both need energy and regulation, but their mechanisms differ. Avoid assuming that a familiar human process is the only way living organisms perform a function.

sections.heading: Connect inheritance and variation
sections.text: Heredity concerns transmission of biological information; variation arises through several processes and interacts with the environment. A trait can have multiple influences, so a simple classroom inheritance example should not be applied to every complex characteristic. Evolution concerns changes in populations over generations, not an individual changing because it wishes to adapt.

sections.heading: Health concepts require distinctions
sections.text: A pathogen, a symptom and a risk factor are different categories. Infectious and non-infectious conditions do not all respond to the same intervention. Vaccination, sanitation, nutrition and surveillance act through different mechanisms. These lessons concern scientific concepts and public systems; use authoritative health sources for current recommendations rather than extending a school-level explanation into personal treatment advice.

rows: Connect structure to a specific function.
Both are relevant to population change.
An effect does not identify its cause by itself.
Defence mechanisms / intervention after or during illness
Different roles should not be conflated.

terms.meaning: A unit of hereditary information in biological context.
Members of a species considered as a group in an area or system.

timeline.event: Relate it to function and regulation.

science-2.trap: Evolution occurs across populations and generations, not as a purposeful change made by an individual.

practice.question: Why should a single-gene classroom example not explain every human characteristic?
practice.answer: Many traits involve multiple genetic influences and environmental interactions. The simplified model illustrates a mechanism but does not establish that all traits follow the same pattern.

mcq: Changes in population characteristics across generations
Evolution concerns heritable population-level change across generations.

science-3.title: Applied science: technology, benefits and limitations

sections.heading: Separate a tool from its application
sections.text: Remote sensing gathers information from a distance, while navigation systems estimate position and timing. Satellites can carry different instruments in different orbits, so the word satellite does not identify a single function. Explain the physical principle and then the use case. For agriculture or disasters, connect the observation to a decision and identify the limits of resolution, timing and interpretation.

sections.heading: Understand a technology chain
sections.text: Biotechnology, semiconductors and digital systems each depend on a sequence of inputs, processes and validation. A laboratory demonstration does not automatically imply an affordable, reliable product at scale. Testing, manufacturing, maintenance and access shape public benefit. Avoid describing a promising technique as a guaranteed solution to every problem in its field.

sections.heading: Evaluate evidence and governance
sections.text: A technology answer needs both mechanism and consequences. Discuss reliability, resource demands, privacy, access and possible misuse where relevant. Artificial-intelligence outputs can contain errors even when fluent; nuclear applications differ between energy, medicine and other fields. Use current official institutional sources for mission details or operational status, while keeping the scientific foundation separate from rapidly changing announcements.

rows: A useful system also needs accessibility and governance.

timeline.event: Connect it to a real public problem.

practice.question: How can satellite images help flood management without replacing local knowledge?
practice.answer: They can reveal inundation and changes over large areas, while local reports identify people, access routes and conditions not captured in an image. Combine timeliness, resolution and ground verification.
